reason: This passage (Exodus 2:16-22) is a narrative account of Moses helping the daughters of the priest of Midian at a well, and subsequently marrying Zipporah. While the text illustrates compassionate action through Moses' intervention—rescuing the women from shepherds and drawing water for their sheep—it contains no explicit statement or indication of Yahweh expressing a desire for the Hebrew people's wellbeing. The passage is focused on Moses' personal circumstances and his integration into a Midianite family, not on any divine declaration regarding Yahweh's will for Hebrew people. No divine voice, command, or stated intention appears in this narrative.
